macro_context.market_sentiment: Risk-off on May 4, 2026: Dow -0.98%, S&P 500 and Nasdaq down ~0.5% as UAE intercepted Iranian missiles, reigniting Strait of Hormuz closure fears. WTI crude surged 4% above $106 and Brent crude +6% above $114, compressing risk appetite across equities.
macro_context.fed_outlook: FOMC held rates at 3.5%-3.75% on April 29, 2026 in an 8-4 split vote — the third consecutive hold after three prior cuts in 2025. Statement flagged elevated inflation partly from rising global energy prices; next cut not priced in until at least September 2026 given Middle East uncertainty.
macro_context.geopolitical: Iran-U.S. military confrontation (intermittent Strait of Hormuz closure) is the dominant risk event of 2026, driving the energy price spike and global growth downgrades. Trump suspended U.S. strikes on Iran for two weeks on May 1, triggering a brief rally; escalation risk remains elevated. Tariff uncertainty, Venezuela intervention, and NATO/Greenland posturing add secondary friction.
key_events: Strait of Hormuz situation — any escalation or re-closure will spike oil further and pressure equities
Fed next meeting (June 2026) — market watching for any shift in easing timeline amid energy-driven inflation
U.S. midterm elections (November 2026) — increasing policy uncertainty
Q2 2026 earnings season (July 2026) — test of how corporates managed energy cost pass-through

Distribution: 8 Buy, 17 Hold, 1 Sell. Seeking Alpha recently downgraded stance to Hold citing market uncertainty. No major upgrades or downgrades from bulge-bracket analysts this week.

web_context.competitor_activity: JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley significantly outperformed Goldman in Q1 2026 fixed income: JPMorgan FICC revenue +21% to $7.1B vs. Goldman FICC -10% (missed by $910M); Morgan Stanley bond revenue +29%. Goldman led North America M&A by value ($267B in Q1), ahead of Morgan Stanley ($210B) and JPMorgan ($207B), suggesting advisory strength offsets trading weakness. Morgan Stanley viewed as cheaper and better diversified via wealth management; JPMorgan remains largest IB by total revenue and poses greatest competitive threat in trading.
